entry.title: docs: document website and desktop regeneration
entry.content:
docs: document website and desktop regeneration

Fill in the Regeneration section of CLAUDE.md and add scripts/ entry
points for the multi-step desktop packaging (adoption steps 6-7):

entry.title: chore: adopt Project Organization Standard layout
entry.content:
chore: adopt Project Organization Standard layout

Move the Cargo workspace under software/ and documentation under docs/
per keel's Project Organization Standard v1.1, and repair everything that
referenced the old root layout:

- CI (ci.yml): run cargo in software/ (working-directory + rust-cache
  workspaces), on both the lint and test jobs.
- Release (release.yml): build in software/; package from
  software/target/release while keeping root-level licenses and docs.
- shiori-gui: re-point the icon include_bytes!/build.rs paths to the
  repo-root assets/ (now one level further up); assets/ stays at root
  because the GitHub-rendered README links it.
- .gitignore: ignore /software/target instead of /target.
- Docs (README, CONTRIBUTING, site architecture/getting-started): build
  commands now cd into software/; crate paths prefixed with software/.
- CLAUDE.md: fill in the project purpose line.

Verified: cargo fmt/clippy(-D warnings)/test --workspace all pass on a
clean build, and `zola build` succeeds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat(app): browse book sources without a search query
entry.content:
feat(app): browse book sources without a search query

Each "Find books online" tab now shows a listing as soon as it opens,
ranked by popularity where the source exposes one.

- Gutenberg: an empty query browses the most-downloaded books, following
  Gutendex's `next` pages to ~100 (default sort is already -download_count).
- Wikisource: browses the most-viewed mainspace works via `list=mostviewed`
  (pageviews), collapsed to whole works, with the Main Page filtered out.
- OPDS: an empty query lists the feed's books, diving one level into a
  popular/most-downloaded subfeed when the root is navigation-only (e.g.
  Project Gutenberg), and reading OPDS 2.0 `groups[]` (e.g. Open Library).
- Aozora: shows the first ~100 catalog works.
- GUI: each tab auto-loads its listing once per (tab, language,
  distributor) with a spinner, and reloads on a switch; Wikisource browse
  rows show "N views/day". Ignored live tests cover all four sources.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: ci: lint on Linux, test on Windows/macOS; drop the Intel macOS build
entry.content:
ci: lint on Linux, test on Windows/macOS; drop the Intel macOS build

- CI: cargo fmt + clippy run once on Linux (clippy also proves the Linux
  build); tests run on Windows and macOS. The release-artifact build no
  longer runs in CI — it is release-only.
- Release: drop the macos-13 (Intel x86_64) target. GitHub's Intel runners
  queue for a very long time and block the whole release; ship Windows,
  Linux, and macOS (Apple Silicon). The redundant fmt/clippy/test steps are
  removed from the release jobs now that CI covers every platform.

ci: run everyday CI on Windows only, validate every platform at release

Cross-platform build+test on every push is expensive. Move the Linux and
macOS validation into the release workflow, which already builds for every
platform on each tag.

- CI (push/PR) is Windows-only again: fmt, clippy, test, release build.
- Each release job now runs fmt/clippy/tests on its own platform before
  building and packaging, so a Linux or macOS break blocks the release
  rather than shipping broken.

entry.title: fix(app): treat Koine and Modern Greek as separate book-search languages
entry.content:
fix(app): treat Koine and Modern Greek as separate book-search languages

Koine (Ancient) Greek no longer borrows the Modern Greek Wikisource — the
only Greek wiki is Modern Greek's and it is not Koine-specific — so Koine
and Modern Greek now share no book sources (like Turkish and French).
Koine keeps its own Project Gutenberg filter (`grc`) and Koine-specific
Libraries directory; Modern Greek keeps `el.wikisource`.

Also rename the Build-from-Wiktionary "Ancient Greek" option to "Koine
Greek" so the language reads as Koine everywhere (the corpus pack, LLM
profile, and catalog already do).

entry.title: feat(app): import whole Wikisource works instead of chapter fragments
entry.content:
feat(app): import whole Wikisource works instead of chapter fragments

Wikisource stores a long book as an index page plus one `Work/Chapter`
subpage per chapter, so search listed every fragment and import fetched
only the thin index page.

- Search collapses subpage hits under their root work, so a book shows
  once with the parts' combined word count and most-relevant snippet.
- Import fetches the whole work as a single EPUB from the Wikimedia
  export tool (the site's "Download as EPUB"), falling back to the
  single page's rendered HTML if the tool is unavailable.

entry.title: feat(gui): per-language book search view with a language switcher
entry.content:
feat(gui): per-language book search view with a language switcher

Rework the "Find books online" view around the active language:

- A language switcher re-scopes every tab and where imports land, and
  clears the previous language's results.
- Tabs adapt to the language: Aozora for Japanese, Wikisource and Project
  Gutenberg where available, OPDS always, and a Libraries directory drawn
  from the bundled catalog.
- OPDS distributors are managed inline (add, remove, one-click
  suggestions), searched per distributor.
- Search results carry the language they were requested for and are
  dropped if the user switches language before they arrive, so a book is
  never shown or imported under the wrong language.

entry.title: feat(app): per-language book search across Wikisource, Gutendex, and …
entry.content:
feat(app): per-language book search across Wikisource, Gutendex, and OPDS

Generalize online book search from Japanese-only to per language.

- Bundle the free digital-libraries catalog and add books.rs, mapping a
  language code to its Wikisource subdomain, Gutendex language filter,
  and catalog section (with region-subtag stripping and Ancient-Greek /
  Norwegian special-casing).
- Wikisource search and import now target the active language's wiki
  instead of a hardcoded ja.wikisource.org.
- Add Gutendex (Project Gutenberg) search and import, filtered to the
  active language, with Gutenberg license boilerplate stripped and
  UTF-8/Latin-1 decoding.
- Add OPDS search and import (opds.rs): OPDS 1.x Atom with OpenSearch
  discovery and one-hop navigation-feed following, plus OPDS 2.0 JSON;
  imports EPUB/PDF/HTML/text. Feed fetching is charset- and size-robust.
- Ignored live smoke tests exercise all four sources against real servers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
